solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Temporary servant in a month turning nit-picky about work

parts.note: MAR is the short form of March

indicators.note: something turning faces the other way, so the word is read back to front
to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: snippy means curt and fault-finding
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A fussy temp spends a month quibbling over the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temporary servant' sounds like an agency temp, but it is the nanny who stays only until the wind changes; 'nit-picky' must be found as a synonym before it is turned.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional nanny arrives with the east wind and leaves when it changes, so she is household help hired only for a while.

clue.text: Soldier in theatre of war once briefly sent back

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: 'Nam is the clipped name for Vietnam, a former war zone

explanation.surface: A veteran is shipped home early from an old war zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' clips Vietnam to its slang short form, which read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A private in the ranks is called one of the men, as in officers and men, so this works as a plain soldier.

clue.text: Paunch of some games players

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a sport
the players on a team are its men

explanation.surface: Sportsmen with beer bellies.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the gut of a team's players; RU is the standard abbreviation for rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoologists call the first stomach of a cow or sheep its paunch, the chamber where grass ferments.

clue.text: Exercise, or call the lift?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gym move pushing the body up from the floor
second meaning: hit the button to summon an elevator heading higher

explanation.walkthrough: A lift is a British elevator; pushing the call button to go up is read as two words, while the gym sense is a hyphenated noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The floor exercise is a push-up, and literally pushing the upward button is how you summon an elevator.

clue.text: Great Khan perhaps to put head round old yurt

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one piece wraps around the others

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
O is the standard abbreviation for old
a yurt is a round felt tent of the Asian steppes

explanation.surface: The Mongol ruler likes to wrap his head around an ancient dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The head word splits round the letters for old and the tent; the Mongol setting of the surface keeps both definition and yurt in one scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A Great Khan was a supreme Mongol ruler, an example of an all-powerful monarch, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Pub should have vermouth, wouldn't you say?

parts.note: an inn is a pub
IT is Italian vermouth, as in the drink gin and it

explanation.surface: Someone insists a decent bar ought to stock vermouth, and seeks agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and it is a British cocktail of gin with Italian (sweet) vermouth, hence IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Innit is slang tag from London speech, a contraction of 'isn't it', asking the listener to agree.

clue.text: Provider, not one to offer more elastic

indicators.note: saying 'not' excludes what follows, so that item is taken away

parts.note: a supplier provides goods
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A supplier declines to put forward any extra stretchy material.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I from SUPPLIER and the comparative adjective is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple means bending easily, and its comparative describes something able to stretch or flex further.

clue.text: First of cold, wet months creating depression in Wales

indicators.note: the first of something is its opening, so only the initial letter of each word counts

parts.note: the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A run of chilly, rainy months makes people in Wales gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks like low mood, which the Welsh weather would explain, but it means a hollow in the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Cwm is the Welsh word for a valley or bowl-shaped hollow in mountains, the same feature as a corrie.

clue.text: At Cambridge, one beginning to learn English singing style

parts.note: Cantab, short for Cantabrigian, denotes Cambridge University, as in degree titles
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of learn

explanation.surface: A student at Cambridge University starts studying English and its manner of singing.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning in a smooth, flowing, song-like way, so a vocal manner.

clue.text: Mediaeval production that might baffle an audience today

definitions.meaning: the setter's reading: a religious drama staged by medieval guilds

definitions.text: that might baffle an audience today
definitions.meaning: the surface reading: a modern whodunit show that keeps viewers puzzled

explanation.walkthrough: The baffling part suggests a modern thriller, but medieval guild dramas of Bible stories carry the same name, from 'mystery' meaning a trade or craft.
explanation.definitionFit: These were cycles of biblical pageants performed by craft guilds in English towns such as York and Chester.

clue.text: Dead tree damaged new leader's address

parts.note: numb means without feeling, dead to sensation

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A fallen tree has ruined a new leader's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a speech the leader gives; it is where the leader lives. Number Ten Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prime Minister of Britain lives and works at Ten Downing Street, so the house number stands for that home.

clue.text: Flowers for half-hearted socialists

definitions.meaning: first meaning: garden plants of the dianthus family
second meaning: people with mild left-wing leanings, short of red

explanation.surface: Someone buys a bouquet for lukewarm left-wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: Red is the colour of committed socialism, so a paler shade suggests only lukewarm sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: The dianthus family includes carnations and clove-scented garden blooms; politically the word labels moderate leftists, diluted reds.

clue.text: Plumber's triumphant call penetrates consciousness

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fitter announcing the basin is installed
second meaning: becomes fully understood, of a realisation

explanation.surface: A plumber's cry of success finally registers with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a shout, the first part is 'Sink's in!' with the apostrophe of 'is'; the second is the phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: When news gradually registers in the mind, people say it has finally been grasped and understood that way.

clue.text: One disclosing strength of alcohol, able to resist a splash

parts.note: someone who shows something reveals it
proof is the measure of a spirit's alcoholic strength

explanation.surface: A label revealing a drink's alcohol content is made to withstand spills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One disclosing' must be read as one who shows, rhyming with mower, not the rainfall word it spells.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing marked this way keeps out light rain, coping with a passing sprinkle though not a downpour.

clue.text: Worked land badly inside broken gate

indicators.note: being inside means enclosed, so this piece sits within another
something broken is smashed apart, so its letters are put together differently

parts.note: taken as written
ill as an adverb means badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A farmer did a poor job ploughing a field behind a broken gate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worked' looks like a verb, but it describes the land as a noun phrase; the ILL piece sits after the T of the rearranged gate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is ground prepared by ploughing for crops, cultivated soil as opposed to pasture.

clue.text: Always available as retiree to tour part of Oz

indicators.note: touring something means going all round it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: OAP stands for old-age pensioner
NT is the Northern Territory of Australia

explanation.surface: A pensioner is always free to travel round Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP is the British term for an old-age pensioner; Oz is Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer drawn from a cask is ready whenever wanted, so the idiom means available at any time.

clue.text: In trip, gas fails, so having weary walk

indicators.note: when something fails it breaks down, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: On a journey the fuel runs out, so everyone has to trudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' is American for petrol, making the surface a car running dry mid-journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to tramp wearily or reluctantly from place to place, so the participle describes trudging along.

clue.text: Hands regularly relax in extremely challenging situation

indicators.note: doing something regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters

indicators.note: to be in something is to be held within it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: very and extremely both intensify
to sit is to rest and relax

explanation.surface: Workers take turns to unwind during a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely challenging' reads as one phrase, but 'extremely' is wordplay and only 'challenging situation' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adversity means hardship or misfortune, a difficult set of circumstances a person must face.

clue.text: Do this, and museum lies in ruins?

parts.note: the Victoria and Albert Museum in London is known as the V and A, written out here as V-AND-A

indicators.note: in ruins means wrecked, so the letters of lies are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that doing this would leave a museum wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: The museum is the V and A, London's Victoria and Albert, read letter for letter; 'in ruins' rearranges LIES to LISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To vandalise is to damage property deliberately, the act that would leave the museum wrecked.

clue.text: Flying team ace, heartless menace in battle

parts.note: El Al is the national airline of Israel
A is the card abbreviation for ace

indicators.note: a thing without a heart has lost its middle, so only its outer letters survive

parts.note: the first and last letters only
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heartless flying ace becomes a menace in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flying team' suggests an air squadron, but it is an airline's crew. 'In' looks like a link to the definition, yet it supplies the last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: El Alamein in Egypt was the site of the decisive 1942 Allied victory over Rommel in the North African campaign.

clue.text: In military base help to guard one grounded

indicators.note: guarding something means standing round it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: aid is help
the rhea is a flightless South American bird, stuck on the ground

explanation.surface: Soldiers at a base help protect a pilot who has been stopped from flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One grounded' suggests a pilot barred from flying, but it is a bird that cannot fly. 'In military' marks the definition as a military usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In military usage this is a secured area in hostile territory where troops and supplies are landed by aircraft, like a beachhead.

clue.text: Get bigger spades to the front of cathedral

indicators.note: only the front of something is its leading portion, so the tail end is dropped

parts.note: Wells is a cathedral city in Somerset, England
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Bigger shovels are needed at the entrance of a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: Spades is a card suit here, not tools; Wells is England's smallest cathedral city, and dropping its last letter leaves its front.
explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to expand or increase in size, as a bruise or a river does.

clue.text: Sort of fever mark on body, half fatal

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: half of something is one of its two equal parts, so the other part is thrown away

parts.note: fatal and lethal both mean deadly

explanation.surface: A feverish illness leaves a mark on the body and is half the time deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap fatal for its synonym lethal before halving it.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet fever is a bacterial illness named for the bright red rash it produces on the skin.

clue.text: Something to read, or reed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an ancient written scroll
second meaning: the tall Nile sedge used to make such scrolls

explanation.walkthrough: The two definitions sound the same when spoken, which tempts a solver to hunt for a sound trick; there is none, only two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Egyptians wrote on sheets made from a water plant, and both the manuscript and the plant share the name.

clue.text: Woman in America opening tin

indicators.note: opening something up lets something else in, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: An American woman opens a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening tin' suggests a can opener, but the tin is the metal's symbol, split apart to take the country inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a common female first name, and crosswords often define given names simply by sex.

clue.text: A drugs officer avoiding conflict wary about heroin leading to disorder

parts.note: taken as written
a narc is an American narcotics agent
H is slang for heroin

indicators.note: avoiding something means staying away from it, so those letters are left out

parts.note: taken as written, before losing the word for conflict
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A narcotics officer, keen to avoid a fight, is cautious about heroin causing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking WAR from wary leaves only Y; heroin's H then goes in front of it, 'leading to' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchy is a state of lawlessness and chaos where no authority keeps order.

clue.text: Crocodile's front leg shows scale

indicators.note: the front of something is its very beginning, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word
a leg is a limb

explanation.surface: A crocodile's foreleg is covered in scales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' looks like the reptile's skin plate, which fits the crocodile, but it is a verb meaning go up.
explanation.definitionFit: To scale a wall or mountain is to ascend it, going upward by hands and feet.

clue.text: Spout, round and long

parts.note: O is round in shape
to pine for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A jug's spout described as rounded and elongated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spout', 'round' and 'long' all look like shape words, as if describing a jug; 'Spout' means to sound off.
explanation.definitionFit: To spout is to hold forth with views, and opining is voicing an opinion, here with a slightly mocking tone.

clue.text: The opposite of a moving picture?

definitions.meaning: the setter's reading: a painting whose subject does not move, such as fruit or flowers in a bowl
the surface reading: a film, as in motion pictures

explanation.walkthrough: A moving picture sounds like a film, or a touching image; the question mark flags the pun, pointing to an artwork of motionless objects.
explanation.definitionFit: This painting genre shows inanimate objects like fruit, jugs and flowers, so nothing in it moves at all.

clue.text: Farm animal seen in the west

indicators.note: something seen in a phrase is visible inside it, so the letters run across the words

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A sheep is spotted out in the west of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a farming observation; the letters straddle the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A female sheep is a familiar livestock creature kept on farms for wool and lambs.

clue.text: Tedious task; one dragged on

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a chore, British slang for a tiresome job
second meaning: a cigarette, which a smoker takes drags on

explanation.surface: A boring chore seemed to go on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang the word means both a wearisome chore ('what a fag') and a cigarette; 'dragged on' suggests time passing slowly, but a drag is a puff.
explanation.definitionFit: British speakers call an irksome job by this slang term, and also use it for a cigarette that one puffs.

clue.text: Entire band gathered round large board

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one piece is wrapped about another
things gathered up are bundled together in a heap, so these letters are regrouped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: The whole group gathers round a big board, perhaps for a meeting or a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like a committee or a game board, but it is the old sense of a table for meals, as in 'bed and board'.
explanation.definitionFit: Board in its old sense is a table where food is served, and the evening meal is eaten at one.
